about: Concept types for the Atlas GUI (redesign.html). Nodes in graph_data.json refer to a type by its id. An entry with a 'parent' nests under that entry, so groups and sub-types can go to any depth; an entry with no nodes of its own acts as a group. Entries without a color, definition, or summary inherit them from their parent. 'summary' phrases the type in the connection summary ({list} = the concepts, {s} = plural ending). 'connectionSentences' are keyed by two type ids joined with '+', in the order the types appear below; sub-types fall back to their parents' sentences. {n} = paper count, {A}/{B} = the two concepts, {a B} = with 'a'/'an'. A 'schema' block inside graph_data.json, if present, takes precedence over this file.

types.label: Subject
types.definition: Agents whose behavior the study was designed to observe.

types.label: Task
types.definition: Activities the subject performs that the study observes.

types.label: Problem
types.definition: Design briefs or prompts given to the subject.

types.label: Construct
types.definition: Cognitive or psychological phenomena the study illuminates.

connectionSentences.task+problem: {n} used {a A} on {a B} design problem
